title: Fishhawk grooming report artifact (plan-stage sibling)
description: The SECOND additive sibling of the plan artifact (after clarification-request-v1), produced by a `plan`-typed PROPOSE stage running the backlog_grooming workflow (ADR-065 §3, ADR-067 §2). Selected over plan-standard-v1 by the top-level 'kind' discriminator BEFORE validation, so plan-standard-v1.schema.json stays frozen. A grooming report is a PROPOSAL, never an applied mutation: it states a proposed ordering with per-item rubric-cited scores, duplicate candidates, hygiene defects, suggested depends_on edges, vision-drift flags, and decomposition suggestions, and a human decides what (if anything) to apply. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT: an ordering entry MUST cite at least one charter rubric line (`rubric_citations` is required with minItems:1), so a ranking that cannot be justified against the charter is REJECTED by this schema rather than merely shipped undecorated — charter §5.1 states the rule, this schema enforces it. Every entry carries a stable `id` DERIVED from the underlying backlog item and proposal class (never minted per run), so two reports over the same backlog diff mechanically run-over-run (#2240). See grooming-report-v1.md for the normative id-derivation contract.

kind.description: Top-level discriminator. The plan package routes an artifact carrying this value to this schema; a clarification_request routes to clarification-request-v1 and anything else (carrying plan_version) to plan-standard-v1. This sibling intentionally omits plan_version so the artifacts never collide on a shared required field.

report_version.description: Artifact schema version, mirroring the plan artifact's plan_version. Single-value enum: a future breaking change bumps to grooming_report_v2 with its own schema file rather than editing this one in place.

summary.description: Human-readable lead paragraph: what backlog slice was groomed, over what window, and the headline of what the report proposes. Rendered first at the operator gate.

charter_ref.description: Optional in grooming_report_v1, INTENDED REQUIRED in the next major: the pinned charter the report was scored against. Left optional here because the charter resolution/injection machinery is E54.2 / #2234's slice and this artifact must not block on it. Draft 2020-12 §10.3 collects x-intended-required as an annotation, so declaring the intent here changes no validation result.

ordering.description: The proposed ranking, one entry per item, each citing at least one charter rubric line. Required and non-empty: a grooming report that proposes no ordering has nothing for the operator to decide. Ranks must be exactly the permutation 1..N (enforced semantically — JSON Schema cannot express it).

duplicates.description: Candidate duplicate/superseded PAIRS (charter S2). Required as an array — an empty array states 'none found', which is a different claim from omitting the key. Never destructive: the report flags the pair and its basis; a human decides.

hygiene_defects.description: Objective, reversible structural defects (charter S4). Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

dependency_edges.description: Suggested depends_on edges between backlog items. DIRECTIONAL: from depends on to. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

vision_drift.description: Items advancing a charter non-goal (§3) or mis-aligned with a phase theme. Charter §5.3: drift is reported as a finding, never quietly ranked last. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

decomposition_suggestions.description: Items the groomer proposes splitting into children. Required as an array; empty states 'none found'.

milestone_scope.description: OPTIONAL (E54.9 / #2309). Present only when the report scopes a release milestone against a human-supplied release definition: the selected, sequenced and excluded backlog items plus the calls it declined to make. Its ABSENCE means this is an ordinary grooming report — additive within the frozen grooming_report_v1 major, so an existing report validates unchanged. A milestone_scope proposes no tracker mutation.

ticket-reference.description: The ticket the grooming RUN was opened against (the run's originating issue), not an item being groomed. Shape mirrors plan-standard-v1 verbatim.

type.description: v0 closed set; v0.x adds linear_ticket and jira_ticket. Mirrors plan-standard-v1.

url.description: Canonical URL of the originating ticket.

agent.description: Agent identifier matching the workflow spec's executor.agent.

version.description: Optional. Model version or build SHA when agent reports it.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of generation. The runner wall-clock at agent invocation.

charter-ref.description: The exact charter revision the report was scored against, so a reviewer can reproduce the scoring and #2240 can tell a genuinely-changed ranking from one that moved because the charter did.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the charter document (e.g. ".fishhawk/charter.md").

content_hash.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the charter bytes the report was scored against.

ref.description: Optional. Git ref or commit SHA the charter was read at.

item-ref.description: A reference to one backlog item. `type` is the PROVIDER DISCRIMINATOR and participates in the derived item-key — identical textual coordinates on two forges are DIFFERENT items and must not collide on one key (see grooming-report-v1.md § Entry-id derivation).

type.description: Provider discriminator. Each admitted value has a defined item-key derivation: github_issue → "github/<id>", gitlab_issue → "gitlab/<id>", jira_issue → "jira/<id>", each lowercased. Never widen this enum without adding the matching derivation case in plan.GroomingEntryID — a value the derivation cannot handle would make the entry id underivable.

id.description: Provider-native stable coordinates: "<owner>/<repo>#<number>" for github_issue, "<namespace>/<project>#<number>" for gitlab_issue, "<PROJECT>-<number>" for jira_issue. The character class EXCLUDES both entry-id separators so the LOWERCASED value is an unambiguous item-key segment: ':' (the class/qualifier separator) and '+' (the pair/edge key separator). Excluding '+' is load-bearing, not cosmetic — a '+' inside a provider-native id would let two DIFFERENT pairs derive the SAME id (see grooming-report-v1.md § Why the item-key alphabet excludes the separators). No admitted provider needs '+'.

url.description: Canonical URL of the backlog item.

entry-id.description: A stable entry id, DERIVED (never minted per run) as `<class>:<item-key>` or `<class>:<item-key>:<qualifier>` or `<class>:<key-a>+<key-b>`, plus the ZERO-REF form `<class>:<qualifier>` a milestone declined call uses (an ambiguous scope question is not necessarily anchored to one item). Lowercase throughout, including the qualifier segment — see grooming-report-v1.md § Entry-id derivation for the normative rules, which the validator machine-checks by recomposing each id from the entry's own fields.

rubric-citation.description: One citation of a charter prioritization-rubric line justifying a score.

rubric_id.description: The charter rubric line id (e.g. "V1", "R3", "U1", "S4"). Charter ids are conventionally uppercase; entry-id qualifiers lowercase them, so charter ids must be CASE-INSENSITIVELY unique.

quote.description: Optional. The cited line's text, so a reviewer can check the citation without opening the charter.

note.description: Optional. Why this line applies to this item.

ordering-entry.description: One item's position in the proposed ranking. `rubric_citations` is REQUIRED with minItems:1 — this is the schema-level enforcement of charter §5.1 ("a score with no citation fails validation"). An entry that omits it, or ships [], is REJECTED; it is never accepted-but-undecorated.

rank.description: 1-based position in the proposed order. Ranks across the ordering array must be exactly the permutation 1..N (enforced semantically).

score.description: The groomer's numeric score. Advisory: the citations, not the number, are what the operator reviews.

rubric_citations.description: At least one charter rubric line justifying this ranking. REQUIRED and minItems:1 — the two together are the citation control.

duplicate-candidate.description: A candidate duplicate/superseded pair (charter S2). UNORDERED: the pair states that two items overlap, with no direction, which is why its id sorts the two item-keys lexicographically.

basis.description: Why the two are believed to overlap. Never destructive — a human decides.

confidence.description: The groomer's confidence in the duplication claim.

hygiene-defect.description: One objective, reversible structural defect on an item (charter S4). Its `fix` is a suggestion rather than a determination: the apply path may refuse a proposed value on containment grounds and record a named skip — notably a proposed `autonomy:` delegation-tier label, which no whole-report approval applies (#2855).

defect.description: Closed set. The value is ALSO this entry's id qualifier, so one item may carry one entry per distinct defect without an id collision.

detail.description: What specifically is missing or wrong.

suggested_fix.description: Optional. PROSE for a human reader, describing the concrete correction proposed. It is NEVER read as a mutation payload: the apply path reads `fix` and nothing else, so an entry whose `fix` is absent applies nothing however precisely this sentence names the value (#2847).

fix.description: Optional. The STRUCTURED mutation payload the apply path reads. Populate exactly the member this entry's `defect` requires: missing_label_namespace -> labels; unlinked_parent_epic / missing_parent_epic_link -> parent_epic; unboarded -> board_state; missing_estimate -> field_value; absent_done_means -> no mechanical mutation, so no fix. An absent, wrong-member or invalid value is recorded as a NAMED skip and applies nothing — it is never recovered from `suggested_fix`, which stays prose for a human.

labels.description: The label names to ADD, each exactly as it must appear on the forge (e.g. `phase:alpha`). No prose, no leading verb, no trailing punctuation, and NO surrounding whitespace — the name is validated exactly as written, never trimmed first: a name carrying whitespace or a control character, beginning or ending with a punctuation/symbol rune, or longer than 50 characters is refused pre-dispatch. This label set is a suggestion rather than a determination. A label in the `autonomy:` DELEGATION-TIER namespace — the label deciding whether an agent may drive the item at all — is NEVER applied under whole-report gate approval or `hygiene: {mode: auto}`: it is recorded as an audited `delegation_tier_not_authorized` skip carrying every proposed label, and needs an explicit per-entry human decision (#2855). One such label refuses the WHOLE entry, so the clerical labels beside it do not land either.

parent_epic.description: The parent epic's issue NUMBER, bare (`389`) or hashed (`#389`). Anything that is not a positive integer after stripping one optional leading `#` is refused pre-dispatch.

board_state.description: The CANONICAL state an unboarded item is placed at (e.g. `backlog`), matched case-insensitively against the work-management conventions `states` map and resolved to that board's own column option before dispatch. A state the conventions do not declare is refused pre-dispatch.

field_value.description: The board field value to write (e.g. an estimate). Single-line; a value carrying a newline is refused pre-dispatch — checked against the value as written, so a LEADING or TRAILING newline is refused too, not trimmed away.

dependency-edge.description: A suggested dependency edge. DIRECTIONAL: `from` depends on `to`. A→B and B→A are DIFFERENT proposals with opposite meaning, so the id encodes from-key then to-key UNSORTED — a sorted derivation would collapse them onto one id, forbidding a report from proposing both directions and hiding a run-over-run edge FLIP as an unchanged id (#2240).

basis.description: Why the dependency is believed to hold.

kind.description: Edge kind. Single-value today; a future major may add blocks/relates_to.

vision-drift-flag.description: An item advancing a charter non-goal or mis-aligned with a phase theme (charter §3 / §5.3).

basis.description: Which charter surface the item drifts from.

charter_ref_id.description: The addressable charter line/theme id (e.g. "NG2", "T4"). This value is ALSO this entry's id qualifier, LOWERCASED — so charter ids must be case-insensitively unique.

detail.description: How the item drifts from the cited line.

decomposition-suggestion.description: A proposal to split one item into children. Proposal only — nothing is filed by this artifact.

rationale.description: Why the item should be split.

proposed_children.description: At least two children — a 'split' into one is not a split.

milestone-scope.description: A scoped, sequenced release milestone (E54.9 / #2309). The class takes a human-supplied release definition and produces the selected items (each with a membership reason and a wave index), the excluded items (each with a reason), the calls it declined to make, a critical path, and its confidence in the prose-derived dependency edges. Seven semantic rules the schema cannot express are machine-checked by plan.ValidateGroomingReport (wave contiguity, dependency resolvability, strict wave monotonicity, out-of-scope dependencies requiring a declined call, critical-path connectivity, declined-call referential integrity, and canonical ordering of every array so identical input yields byte-identical output). Proposes no tracker mutation.

included.description: The items scoped INTO the milestone, each with a membership reason and a wave index. minItems:0 — an empty scoped set is a real, different claim from an absent milestone_scope key. Sorted by (wave, item key) — canonical ordering, enforced semantically.

excluded.description: The items scoped OUT, each with a reason and a rubric citation. Sorted by item key (enforced semantically).

declined_calls.description: The ambiguous scope questions the class REFUSED to resolve, surfaced for an operator rather than guessed. REQUIRED and may be empty: an empty array states 'nothing was ambiguous', an absent key states nothing at all. Sorted by question_id (enforced semantically).

critical_path.description: The longest dependency chain through the milestone, as an ORDERED sequence of item keys. Each consecutive pair MUST be connected by a declared depends_on edge (element i+1 depends on element i), so the sequence is a real path through the graph rather than unrelated items in increasing waves — enforced semantically. Order is meaningful, so this array is NOT canonicalized by sorting.

release-definition.description: The human-supplied release definition the milestone is scoped against. The class must NEVER invent this — the only admitted provenance names the human.

label.description: Short human name for the milestone (e.g. "alpha", "v0.3").

text.description: The release definition as the operator supplied it — the fuzzy prose the class scopes against.

source.description: Provenance. Single-value enum: the release definition is a human input, never derived, so the only admitted source names the operator.

milestone-framing.description: How the class framed the milestone: the step most likely to be plausible-and-wrong, so it is stated explicitly and grounded.

statement.description: The framing the class adopted — what it took the milestone to mean before scoping items into it.

basis.description: The architectural anchor for the framing — an ADR, an architecture-doc section, or a charter line — so a reviewer can check the framing against something concrete.

milestone-inclusion.description: One item scoped INTO the milestone. `reason` and `rubric_citations` are the legibility control (criteria 1 and 3): a bare list is unexpressible.

reason.description: Why this item is in the milestone. Non-empty by construction.

wave.description: The 0-based DAG layer this item sits in. Waves across `included` must be exactly the contiguous set 0..K (enforced semantically), so the assignment describes an executable sequence.

depends_on.description: Item keys this inclusion depends on. Each must resolve to an item in `included` or `excluded` (enforced semantically). Sorted (canonical ordering, enforced semantically).

open_question_ids.description: The declined_calls[].question_id values this inclusion is contingent on — e.g. when it depends on an out-of-scope item, the ambiguity that was declined rather than resolved silently. Each must match some declined_calls[].question_id (enforced semantically). Sorted (canonical ordering).

rubric_citations.description: At least one charter rubric line grounding the inclusion — the same citation control #2235 applies to ordering entries. REQUIRED with minItems:1. Sorted by rubric_id (canonical ordering).

milestone-exclusion.description: One item scoped OUT of the milestone. `rubric_citations` is REQUIRED on the SAME terms as an inclusion: "why is E61 out of alpha" needs the same grounding as why something is in, or the exclusion is the taste argument the charter rubric exists to prevent (approval condition C2).

reason.description: Why this item is excluded. Non-empty by construction.

rubric_citations.description: At least one charter rubric line grounding the exclusion. REQUIRED with minItems:1 (C2). Sorted by rubric_id (canonical ordering).

milestone-declined-call.description: One ambiguous scope question the class REFUSED to resolve. Mirrors the clarification_request question shape so an operator can answer it. `rubric_citations` is REQUIRED on the same terms as inclusions/exclusions (C2).

question_id.description: A stable id for the question. This value, LOWERCASED, is the entry id's zero-ref qualifier (`milestone_declined:<lowercased question_id>`), so it must be case-insensitively unique across declined_calls.

question.description: The ambiguous question, phrased for an operator to answer.

why_ambiguous.description: Why the class could not resolve it from the release definition alone. Non-empty by construction.

recommended_default.description: Optional. The answer the class would pick if forced, so an operator can accept it in one step.

options.description: Optional. The candidate answers. Sorted (canonical ordering).

item_refs.description: Optional. The backlog items the question bears on. Sorted by item key (canonical ordering).

rubric_citations.description: At least one charter rubric line grounding why this call matters. REQUIRED with minItems:1 (C2). Sorted by rubric_id (canonical ordering).

item-key.description: A derived, lowercased item key of the form `<provider>/<id>` (e.g. `github/kuhlman-labs/fishhawk#2235`) — the same key plan.itemKey derives from an item_ref. Used as a graph reference in a milestone's depends_on and critical_path.

edge-confidence.description: The class's confidence in the dependency edges it derived, since a milestone's edges are typically read out of prose rather than declared.

level.description: How much to trust the edges: high (declared depends_on), medium (strongly implied by prose), low (inferred).

basis.description: Why that confidence level — e.g. "edges read from issue bodies, not declared depends_on links".
